```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD AND PREPARE THE DATA
# ============================================================

Df_table2 <- read_csv(
  "Df_clean.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    id_strategy = case_when(
      is.na(id_strategy) | id_strategy == "" ~ NA_character_,
      id_strategy %in% c("OLS", "IV") ~ id_strategy,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    
    # 1 if no fixed effects are included; 0 if at least one is included
    no_FE = case_when(
      if_all(
        all_of(c("worker_FE", "localisation_FE", "time_FE", "firm_FE")),
        ~ !is.na(.x) & .x == 0
      ) ~ 1,
      if_any(
        all_of(c("worker_FE", "localisation_FE", "time_FE", "firm_FE")),
        ~ .x == 1
      ) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # Indicators for absence of controls
    no_weather_controls = case_when(
      controls_weather == 0 ~ 1,
      controls_weather == 1 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    no_multiple_pollutants = case_when(
      controls_multipollutant == 0 ~ 1,
      controls_multipollutant == 1 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # Aggregation level: keep Indiv and Firm; all other levels -> Other
    outcome_level = case_when(
      is.na(outcome_level) | str_trim(as.character(outcome_level)) == "" ~ NA_character_,
      str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(outcome_level))) %in%
        c("worker", "individual", "individual level") ~ "Worker",
      str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(outcome_level))) %in%
        c("firm", "firm level") ~ "Firm",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    
    # Frequency: keep Daily and Yearly; all other frequencies -> Other
    time_frequency_observation = case_when(
      is.na(time_frequency_observation) |
        str_trim(as.character(time_frequency_observation)) == "" ~ NA_character_,
      str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(time_frequency_observation))) == "daily" ~ "Daily",
      str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(time_frequency_observation))) == "yearly" ~ "Yearly",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    
    # Any weather controls other than temperature, wind speed and humidity
    weather_other = case_when(
      if_any(
        all_of(c(
          "control_precipitation",
          "control_radiation",
          "control_wind_direction",
          "control_air_pressure",
          "control_snow",
          "control_dew_points",
          "control_skycover",
          "control_sunshine"
        )),
        ~ !is.na(.x) & .x == 1
      ) ~ 1,
      if_all(
        all_of(c(
          "control_precipitation",
          "control_radiation",
          "control_wind_direction",
          "control_air_pressure",
          "control_snow",
          "control_dew_points",
          "control_skycover",
          "control_sunshine"
        )),
        ~ !is.na(.x) & .x == 0
      ) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(study_id)) |>
  group_by(study_id) |>
  mutate(weight = 1 / n()) |>
  ungroup()

# Standard-error column
se_col <- "se_elasticity"

if (!se_col %in% names(Df_table2)) {
  stop("The column 'se_elasticity' was not found in Df_table2.")
}


# ============================================================
# 1bis. REMOVE THE TOP AND BOTTOM 5% OF ELASTICITIES
# ============================================================

# Ensure elasticity is numeric
Df_table2 <- Df_table2 |>
  mutate(elasticity = as.numeric(elasticity))

# Calculate the 5th and 95th percentiles
elasticity_limits <- quantile(
  Df_table2$elasticity,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95),
  na.rm = TRUE,
  names = FALSE
)

lower_bound <- elasticity_limits[1]
upper_bound <- elasticity_limits[2]

# Keep only elasticities between the two thresholds
n_before <- nrow(Df_table2)

Df_table2 <- Df_table2 |>
  filter(
    is.finite(elasticity),
    elasticity >= lower_bound,
    elasticity <= upper_bound
  ) |>
  group_by(study_id) |>
  mutate(weight = 1 / n()) |>
  ungroup()

n_after <- nrow(Df_table2)

# Report the thresholds and number of observations removed
cat("5th percentile:", lower_bound, "\n")
cat("95th percentile:", upper_bound, "\n")
cat("Observations before trimming:", n_before, "\n")
cat("Observations after trimming:", n_after, "\n")
cat("Observations removed:", n_before - n_after, "\n")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

# ============================================================
# A. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# 2. DEFINE VARIABLES AND CATEGORIES
# ============================================================

groups <- tribble(
  ~variable, ~subcategory, ~order,
  "data_country", "Country", 1,
  "development", "Development level", 2,
  "urban_rural", "Localisation (urban / rural)", 3,
  "indoor_outdoor", "Indoor or outdoor workers", 4,
  "age_mean", "Mean Age", 5,
  "pct_female", "Female", 6,
  
  "sector", "Sector", 7,
  "task_type", "Task type", 8,
  "outcome_category", "Productivity measures", 9,
  "outcome_level", "Aggregation level", 10,
  
  "pollutant", "Pollution measures", 11,
  "exposure_measure", "Pollution method measurement", 12,
  
  "data_structure", "Data structure", 13,
  "time_frequency_observation", "Frequency", 14,
  "effect_type_raw", "Estimation method", 15,
  "id_strategy", "Identification strategy", 16,
  
  "time_FE", "Fixed effects", 17,
  "worker_FE", "Fixed effects", 17,
  "firm_FE", "Fixed effects", 17,
  "localisation_FE", "Fixed effects", 17,
  "no_FE", "Fixed effects", 17,
  
  "controls_weather", "Weather controls", 18,
  "control_temp", "Weather controls", 18,
  "control_wind_speed", "Weather controls", 18,
  "control_humidity", "Weather controls", 18,
  "weather_other", "Weather controls", 18,
  "no_weather_controls", "Weather controls", 18,
  
  "controls_multipollutant", "Other pollutant controls", 19,
  "no_multiple_pollutants", "Other pollutant controls", 19,
  
  "controls_worker_characteristics", "Other controls", 20,
  "attendance_bias_treated", "Other controls", 20,
  "controls_traffic_effect", "Other controls", 20,
  "controls_demand_effect", "Other controls", 20,
  "controls_wage_shirking", "Other controls", 20
)

# ============================================================
# 3. DEFINE VARIABLE TYPES
# ============================================================

num <- c("age_mean", "pct_female")

dummy_groups <- c(
  "Fixed effects",
  "Weather controls",
  "Other pollutant controls",
  "Other controls"
)

dummy <- groups |>
  filter(subcategory %in% dummy_groups) |>
  pull(variable)

cat <- groups |>
  filter(!variable %in% c(num, dummy)) |>
  pull(variable)

# Detect potential mismatch between Df_table2 and groups
missing_variables <- setdiff(groups$variable, names(Df_table2))

if (length(missing_variables) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The following variables are missing from Df_table2: ",
    paste(missing_variables, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# ============================================================
# 4. VARIABLE LABELS
# ============================================================

variable_labels <- c(
  data_country = "Country",
  development = "Development level",
  urban_rural = "Localisation (urban / rural)",
  indoor_outdoor = "Indoor or outdoor workers",
  sector = "Sector",
  task_type = "Task type",
  outcome_category = "Productivity measures",
  outcome_level = "Aggregation level",
  exposure_measure = "Pollution method measurement",
  data_structure = "Data structure",
  time_frequency_observation = "Frequency",
  age_mean = "Mean Age",
  pct_female = "Female",
  
  pollutant = "Pollution measures",
  effect_type_raw = "Estimation method",
  id_strategy = "Identification strategy",
  
  time_FE = "Time FE",
  worker_FE = "Worker FE",
  firm_FE = "Firm FE",
  localisation_FE = "Localisation FE",
  no_FE = "No fixed effects",
  
  controls_weather = "Weather controls",
  no_weather_controls = "No weather controls",
  control_temp = "Temperature",
  control_wind_speed = "Wind speed",
  control_humidity = "Humidity",
  weather_other = "Other",
  
  controls_multipollutant = "Multiple pollutants",
  no_multiple_pollutants = "No multiple pollutants",
  
  controls_worker_characteristics = "Worker characteristics",
  attendance_bias_treated = "Attendance bias",
  controls_traffic_effect = "Traffic controls",
  controls_demand_effect = "Demand controls",
  controls_wage_shirking = "Wage / shirking controls"
)

# ============================================================
# 5. STATISTICS FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================

elasticity_col <- "elasticity"

if (!elasticity_col %in% names(Df_table2)) {
  stop("The column '", elasticity_col, "' was not found in Df_table2.")
}

weighted_mean_safe <- function(x, w) {
  valid <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  if (!any(valid)) return(NA_real_)
  weighted.mean(x[valid], w[valid])
}

mean_safe <- function(v) if (length(v) > 0) mean(v) else NA_real_
sd_safe   <- function(v) if (length(v) > 1) sd(v) else NA_real_
min_safe  <- function(v) if (length(v) > 0) min(v) else NA_real_
max_safe  <- function(v) if (length(v) > 0) max(v) else NA_real_

calc_stats <- function(x, data, scale = 100, elasticity_stats = TRUE) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  elas <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data[[elasticity_col]]))
  se <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data[[se_col]]))
  
  valid_x <- is.finite(x)
  in_cat <- if (elasticity_stats) valid_x & x == 1 else rep(FALSE, length(x))
  e <- elas[in_cat & is.finite(elas)]
  s <- se[in_cat & is.finite(se)]
  
  tibble(
    pct_estimates = scale * mean_safe(x[valid_x]),
    pct_studies = scale * weighted_mean_safe(x, data$weight),
    elas_mean = if (elasticity_stats) mean_safe(e) else NA_real_,
    elas_sd = if (elasticity_stats) sd_safe(e) else NA_real_,
    elas_min = if (elasticity_stats) min_safe(e) else NA_real_,
    elas_max = if (elasticity_stats) max_safe(e) else NA_real_,
    se_mean = if (elasticity_stats) mean_safe(s) else NA_real_,
    se_sd = if (elasticity_stats) sd_safe(s) else NA_real_
  )
}

# ============================================================
# 6. STATISTICS BY VARIABLE TYPE
# ============================================================

thermal_pattern <- "thermal"

# Subrows among IV estimates
iv_rows <- function(data) {
  d <- data |>
    filter(id_strategy == "IV") |>
    group_by(study_id) |>
    mutate(weight = 1 / n()) |>
    ungroup()
  
  thermal <- str_detect(
    coalesce(as.character(d$instrument_type), ""),
    regex(thermal_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)
  )
  
  bind_rows(
    bind_cols(
      tibble(
        Variable = "id_strategy",
        Category = "Thermal inversion",
        Level = 1L,
        Sub_rank = 1L
      ),
      calc_stats(as.numeric(thermal), d)
    ),
    bind_cols(
      tibble(
        Variable = "id_strategy",
        Category = "Other instrument",
        Level = 1L,
        Sub_rank = 2L
      ),
      calc_stats(as.numeric(!thermal), d)
    )
  )
}

stats_variable <- function(v, data) {
  if (v %in% num) {
    return(
      bind_cols(
        tibble(Variable = v, Category = ""),
        calc_stats(data[[v]], data, scale = 1, elasticity_stats = FALSE)
      )
    )
  }
  
  if (v %in% dummy) {
    category_label <- case_when(
      v == "no_FE" ~ "No fixed effects",
      v == "no_weather_controls" ~ "No weather controls",
      v == "no_multiple_pollutants" ~ "No multiple pollutants",
      TRUE ~ "Yes (= 1)"
    )
    
    # These four weather-detail rows are indented.
    # "No weather controls" remains unindented and appears last.
    weather_details <- c(
      "control_temp",
      "control_wind_speed",
      "control_humidity",
      "weather_other"
    )
    
    is_weather_detail <- v %in% weather_details
    
    return(
      bind_cols(
        tibble(
          Variable = v,
          Category = if (is_weather_detail) {
            unname(variable_labels[v])
          } else {
            category_label
          },
          Level = if (is_weather_detail) 1L else 0L,
          Sub_rank = case_when(
            v == "control_temp" ~ 1L,
            v == "control_wind_speed" ~ 2L,
            v == "control_humidity" ~ 3L,
            v == "weather_other" ~ 4L,
            v == "no_weather_controls" ~ 5L,
            TRUE ~ 0L
          )
        ),
        calc_stats(data[[v]], data)
      )
    )
  }
  
  # Categorical variable: one row per category
  values <- as.character(data[[v]])
  values[is.na(values) | values == ""] <- "NA"
  
  out <- map_dfr(unique(values), function(mod) {
    bind_cols(
      tibble(Variable = v, Category = mod),
      calc_stats(as.numeric(values == mod), data)
    )
  })
  
  # Subrows under IV
  if (v == "id_strategy") out <- bind_rows(out, iv_rows(data))
  
  out
}

# ============================================================
# 7. BUILD THE RESULT ROWS
# ============================================================

groups_pos <- groups |>
  mutate(
    pos = row_number(),
    block = match(subcategory, unique(subcategory))
  ) |>
  select(variable, subcategory, pos, block)

clean_label <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  paste0(toupper(substr(x, 1, 1)), substr(x, 2, nchar(x)))
}

results <- map_dfr(groups$variable, stats_variable, data = Df_table2) |>
  left_join(groups_pos, by = c("Variable" = "variable")) |>
  mutate(
    Level = coalesce(Level, 0L),
    Sub_rank = coalesce(Sub_rank, 0L),
    Variable_label = coalesce(unname(variable_labels[Variable]), Variable),
    Row_label = if_else(
      Category %in% c("", "Yes (= 1)"),
      Variable_label,
      Category
    ),
    Row_label = clean_label(Row_label)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    iv_pct = pct_estimates[Variable == "id_strategy" & Category == "IV"][1],
    sort_pct = if_else(Level == 1L, iv_pct, pct_estimates)
  ) |>
  arrange(block, pos, desc(sort_pct), Sub_rank)

# ============================================================
# 8. ADD CATEGORY HEADERS
# ============================================================

stat_cols <- c(
  "pct_estimates", "pct_studies",
  "elas_mean", "elas_sd", "elas_min", "elas_max",
  "se_mean", "se_sd"
)

results <- results |>
  group_by(block) |>
  mutate(has_header = !(n() == 1 & Row_label == first(subcategory))) |>
  ungroup()

result_rows <- results |>
  mutate(
    is_header = !has_header,
    row_order = row_number(),
    Characteristic = case_when(
      Level == 1L ~ paste0("   ", strrep("\u00A0", 6), Row_label),
      has_header ~ paste0("   ", Row_label),
      TRUE ~ Row_label
    )
  ) |>
  select(block, Characteristic, is_header, row_order, all_of(stat_cols))

header_rows <- results |>
  filter(has_header) |>
  group_by(block) |>
  summarise(
    Characteristic = first(subcategory),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    results |>
      group_by(block) |>
      summarise(first_result_row = min(row_number()), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "block"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_header = TRUE,
    row_order = first_result_row - 0.5
  ) |>
  select(block, Characteristic, is_header, row_order)

first_row <- result_rows |>
  group_by(block) |>
  summarise(first_order = min(row_order), .groups = "drop")

header_rows <- header_rows |>
  select(-row_order) |>
  left_join(first_row, by = "block") |>
  mutate(row_order = first_order - 0.5) |>
  select(-first_order)

Table2_display <- bind_rows(header_rows, result_rows) |>
  arrange(row_order) |>
  select(Characteristic, is_header, all_of(stat_cols))

# ============================================================
# 9. FORMAT THE TABLE WITH GT
# ============================================================

Table2_gt <- Table2_display |>
  gt(rowname_col = "Characteristic") |>
  cols_hide(columns = is_header) |>
  cols_label(
    pct_estimates = "% of estimates",
    pct_studies = "% of studies",
    elas_mean = "Mean elasticity",
    elas_sd = "SD elasticity",
    elas_min = "Min",
    elas_max = "Max",
    se_mean = "Mean (SE)",
    se_sd = "SD (SE)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(pct_estimates, pct_studies), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      elas_mean, elas_sd, elas_min, elas_max,
      se_mean, se_sd
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  sub_missing(columns = everything(), missing_text = "") |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_stub(rows = is_header)
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(
      sides = "left",
      color = "#D3D3D3",
      weight = px(2)
    ),
    locations = cells_body(columns = elas_mean)
  ) |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = 11,
    data_row.padding = px(3),
    stub.border.style = "solid",
    stub.border.width = px(2),
    stub.border.color = "#D3D3D3"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    "Note: under IV, the shares are computed among IV estimates only."
  )

# ============================================================
# 10. EXPORT AND DISPLAY
# ============================================================

Table2_gt
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# B. DENSITY OF ELASTICITIES
# ============================================================

# Reuse the database already trimmed at the 5th and 95th percentiles
Df_plot <- Df_table2 |>
  filter(is.finite(elasticity))

# ============================================================
# Plot 1: Unweighted histogram + density curve
# ============================================================

p_density <- ggplot(Df_plot, aes(x = elasticity)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 50,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of estimated elasticities",
    subtitle = paste("N =", nrow(Df_plot), "estimates"),
    x = "Elasticity",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_density)

# ============================================================
# Plot 2: Elasticity density weighted by 1/n_j
# ============================================================

Df_weighted <- Df_plot |>
  group_by(study_id) |>
  mutate(
    weight = 1 / n()
  ) |>
  ungroup()

p_density_weighted <- ggplot(
  Df_weighted,
  aes(x = elasticity, weight = weight)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 50,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of estimated elasticities",
    subtitle = "Weighted by the inverse number of estimates per study",
    x = "Elasticity",
    y = "Density",
    caption = "Each study receives a total weight of 1."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_density_weighted)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# C. DENSITY OF ABSOLUTE T-STATISTICS
# ============================================================

# 1. Calculate absolute t-statistics
Df_tstat <- Df_table2 |>
  filter(
    is.finite(elasticity),
    is.finite(se_elasticity),
    se_elasticity > 0
  ) |>
  mutate(t_stat = abs(elasticity / se_elasticity)) |>
  filter(t_stat <= 25)

# ============================================================
# Plot 1: Unweighted histogram + density curve
# ============================================================

p_tstat <- ggplot(Df_tstat, aes(x = t_stat)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 50,
    fill = "grey80",
    color = "grey60",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_density(
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1.1,
    adjust = 1
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1.96,
    color = "#8B1A1A",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1.96,
    y = Inf,
    label = "1.96",
    color = "#8B1A1A",
    vjust = 1.5,
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 25),
    breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of absolute t-statistics",
    subtitle = paste("N =", nrow(Df_tstat), "estimates"),
    x = "Unweighted |t|-statistics",
    y = "Density",
    caption = "Estimates with |t| > 25 are excluded."
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p_tstat)

# ============================================================
# Plot 2: Density weighted by 1/n_j
# ============================================================

Df_tstat_weighted <- Df_tstat |>
  group_by(study_id) |>
  mutate(weight = 1 / n()) |>
  ungroup()

p_tstat_weighted <- ggplot(
  Df_tstat_weighted,
  aes(x = t_stat, weight = weight)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 50,
    fill = "grey80",
    color = "grey60",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_density(
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1.1,
    adjust = 1
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1.96,
    color = "#8B1A1A",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1.96,
    y = Inf,
    label = "1.96",
    color = "#8B1A1A",
    vjust = 1.5,
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 25),
    breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of absolute t-statistics",
    subtitle = "Weighted by the inverse number of estimates per study",
    x = "Weighted |t|-statistics",
    y = "Density",
    caption = "Each study receives a total weight of 1; estimates with |t| > 25 are excluded."
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p_tstat_weighted)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# D. ELASTICITIES BY STUDY — UNWEIGHTED
#   1. Boxplot
#   2. Mean elasticity + 95% CI
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# Graph theme
# ============================================================

theme_graph <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Times New Roman") +
    theme(
      # Titles
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 14,
        face = "bold",
        colour = "#1F1F1F",
        hjust = 0
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 11,
        colour = "grey35",
        hjust = 0
      ),

      # Axes
      axis.title = element_text(
        size = 11,
        colour = "#1F1F1F"
      ),
      axis.text = element_text(
        size = 9,
        colour = "#333333"
      ),

      # Grid
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),

      # Legend
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),

      # Caption
      plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 8,
        colour = "grey40",
        hjust = 0
      ),

      # Margins
      plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
    )
}

# ============================================================
# Function: format study references
# ============================================================

make_label <- function(id) {
  year <- stringr::str_extract(id, "[0-9]{4}[a-z]?$")
  name <- stringr::str_remove(id, "[0-9]{4}[a-z]?$")
  name <- stringr::str_replace(name, "EtAl$", " et al.")
  paste0(name, " (", year, ")")
}

# 1. Prepare data
Df_study <- Df_table2 |>
  filter(
    !is.na(study_id),
    is.finite(elasticity)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    el = as.numeric(elasticity),
    se = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(se_elasticity)),
    se = if_else(is.finite(se) & se > 0, se, NA_real_),
    dof_ = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(dof)),
    crit = if_else(
      is.finite(dof_) & dof_ > 0,
      qt(0.975, dof_),
      qnorm(0.975)
    ),
    label = make_label(study_id)
  )

# Order studies by label
study_levels <- Df_study |>
  distinct(label) |>
  arrange(label) |>
  pull(label)

Df_study <- Df_study |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rev(study_levels)))

# ============================================================
# Plot 1: Boxplot of individual elasticities by study
# ============================================================

p_box_unweighted <- ggplot(
  Df_study,
  aes(x = el, y = label)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "white",
    colour = "#1F4E79",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    outlier.size = 1.2,
    width = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(8)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of elasticities by study",
    subtitle = "Unweighted estimates",
    x = "Elasticity",
    y = "Reference",
    caption = paste(
      "Boxes: first and third quartiles; central line: median;",
      "whiskers: up to 1.5 x IQR; dots: outliers."
    )
  ) +
  theme_graph()

print(p_box_unweighted)

# ============================================================
# Plot 2: Mean elasticity by study + 95% CI
# ============================================================

study_means_unweighted <- Df_study |>
  group_by(study_id, label) |>
  summarise(
    n_estimates = sum(is.finite(el)),
    mean = mean(el, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_el = if (sum(is.finite(el)) > 1) {
      sd(el, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    se_mean = sd_el / sqrt(n_estimates),
    crit_mean = if (n_estimates > 1) {
      qt(0.975, n_estimates - 1)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    mean_low = mean - crit_mean * se_mean,
    mean_high = mean + crit_mean * se_mean,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_mean_ci_unweighted <- ggplot(
  study_means_unweighted,
  aes(y = label)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(xmin = mean_low, xmax = mean_high),
    orientation = "y",
    colour = "#1F4E79",
    linewidth = 0.5,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = mean),
    shape = 18,
    size = 2.6,
    colour = "#1F4E79"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(8)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean elasticity by study",
    subtitle = "Unweighted mean with 95% confidence interval",
    x = "Mean elasticity",
    y = "Reference",
    caption = paste(
      "Diamonds: arithmetic mean of elasticities within each study.",
      "Bars: 95% confidence intervals based on the within-study SD."
    )
  ) +
  theme_graph()

print(p_mean_ci_unweighted)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Plot 3: Funnel plot
# ============================================================

Df_funnel <- Df_study |>
  filter(
    is.finite(el),
    is.finite(se),
    se > 0
  )

# Overall mean elasticity
mean_elasticity <- mean(Df_funnel$el, na.rm = TRUE)

p_funnel <- ggplot(
  Df_funnel,
  aes(x = el, y = se)
) +
  # Vertical line: overall mean elasticity
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_elasticity,
    linetype = "solid",
    colour = "#C0504D",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  # Funnel limits: approximate 95% reference boundaries
  geom_line(
    data = tibble(
      se = seq(0, max(Df_funnel$se, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 200)
    ) |>
      mutate(
        left = mean_elasticity - 1.96 * se,
        right = mean_elasticity + 1.96 * se
      ) |>
      pivot_longer(
        cols = c(left, right),
        names_to = "boundary",
        values_to = "el"
      ),
    aes(x = el, y = se, group = boundary),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#1F4E79",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(
    colour = "#1F4E79",
    alpha = 0.65,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(6)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(8)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Funnel plot of elasticity estimates",
    subtitle = "Unweighted estimates",
    x = "Elasticity",
    y = "Standard error",
    caption = paste(
      "Vertical line: mean elasticity.",
      "Dashed lines: approximate 95% reference boundaries."
    )
  ) +
  theme_graph()

print(p_funnel)
```
